text: Acts as a drop-in replacement for npm on existing projects, no migration or lockfile rewrites needed
quote: pnpm is a drop-in replacement for npm — and then keeps going, with the features large repos actually need.

text: Lets you patch a dependency's code with a persistent patch reapplied on every install
quote: Fix a bug in a package without waiting for upstream — "pn patch" writes a persistent patch that is reapplied on every install.

text: Can install and pin a specific Node.js version per project directly from pnpm
quote: Install and pin Node.js per project straight from pnpm — no nvm, no shell hooks, no “works on my machine” version mismatches.

text: Only explicitly declared dependencies are accessible from node_modules, preventing phantom imports
quote: Only your declared dependencies land in the root of node_modules, so your code can never quietly import a package you never installed.

text: First-class monorepo support with workspace protocol, task filtering, and one shared lockfile
quote: First-class monorepos: the workspace protocol for local packages, filtering to run tasks on just the projects you touched, and a single lockfile for everything.

text: Catalogs let you define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reuse it everywhere
quote: Define a dependency version once in pnpm-workspace.yaml and reference it as "catalog:" everywhere. One line to upgrade, and no more version-drift merge conflicts.

text: The workspace: protocol only resolves to local workspace packages, never falling back to the registry
quote: pnpm supports the workspace: protocol. When this protocol is used, pnpm will refuse to resolve to anything other than a local workspace package.

text: Dry-run mode resolves dependencies and reports what an install would change without writing to disk
quote: Run a full dependency resolution and report what a real install would change, without writing anything to disk.

text: Offline install mode uses only packages already in the local store and fails if any are missing
quote: If true, pnpm will use only packages already available in the store. If a package won't be found locally, the installation will fail.

text: Verifies ECDSA registry signatures of installed packages against registry public keys
quote: Verifies the ECDSA registry signatures of installed packages against the public keys published by each registry at `/-/npm/v1/keys`.

text: Supports dependency overrides in pnpm-workspace.yaml to force non-vulnerable versions
quote: Add overrides to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` file in order to force non-vulnerable versions of the dependencies.

text: Automatically switches to frozen-lockfile mode when running in CI
quote: When pnpm detects that it is running in CI, it switches to frozen-lockfile mode automatically.

text: Supports per-workspace-package configuration settings, replacing per-project .npmrc files
quote: Allows setting project-specific configuration for individual workspace packages. This replaces workspace project-specific `.npmrc` files.

text: Uses a shared content-addressable store with hard links so identical package versions are stored once on disk
quote: Files inside node_modules are hard-linked from a single content-addressable store. A hundred projects on the same version cost you one copy on disk.

text: Requires explicit approval before a package's install/build scripts are allowed to run
quote: Install scripts don't run for arbitrary dependencies. You approve which packages may execute build scripts — supply-chain safety without extra tooling.

text: Lets workspace packages depend on each other locally while still publishing to a remote registry without extra publish steps
quote: This feature allows you to depend on your local workspace packages while still being able to publish the resulting packages to the remote registry without needing intermediary publish steps

text: Provides a `pnpm licenses list` command to inspect dependency licenses
quote: pnpm supports it via `pnpm licenses list`.

text: Ships as a self-contained executable that needs no pre-installed Node.js and can install a runtime afterward
quote: It needs no Node.js. pnpm is a self-contained executable, and it can install the runtime for you afterwards with `pnpm runtime set node lts -g`

text: Automatically switches to the Node/pnpm version declared in package.json's packageManager field
quote: If your `package.json` has a `packageManager` or `devEngines.packageManager` field, pnpm switches to that version on first use

text: Can skip fetching runtime entries during install while leaving the lockfile untouched for frozen installs
quote: Skip installing runtime entries (e.g. Node.js downloaded via `devEngines.runtime`). The lockfile is left untouched, so frozen installs still validate; only the runtime fetch and bin-linking are skipped.

text: Checks installed packages for known security vulnerabilities
quote: Checks for known security issues with the installed packages.

text: Publishes benchmark results claiming up to 2x faster installs than alternative package managers
quote: Up to 2x faster than the alternatives (see [benchmark](#benchmark)).

text: Can function as a Node.js version manager
quote: Works as a Node.js version manager.
